Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise package addressing each item; I also attached a short overview and the internal dashboard access instructions.

1) Definitions & measurement\- Availability: percentage of successful host-level API responses over total requests, measured at the edge load balancer. Window: 30-day rolling window for formal SLO calculations; 1-hour/6-hour windows used for monitoring and alerting.
\- Latency: p95/p99 measured on server-side response-complete timestamps (request received -> final byte sent). Percentiles computed from aggregated traces every minute and rolled up into the 30-day and 7-day views.

2) Access to raw metrics/dashboard\- We host customer-facing dashboards in a read-only Redshifts-backed Grafana workspace. For Acme Health we can provision:
  * Full read-only dashboard access to the SLO workspace (queries, panels)
  * A filtered view scoped to your tenant id (no cross-customer traces)
  * Audit logging of who viewed/exported reports

See attached: dashboard-access-instructions.md (contains IAM role names and steps).

3) Alerting & on-call commitments\- Standard alerting thresholds (hosted API):
  * p99 latency spike: alert at sustained >2x baseline for 15 minutes
  * error rate: alert at >0.5% errors sustained >5 minutes
  * availability drops below SLO target: immediate paging to on-call
\- Our incident response: initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes, triage within 60 minutes for production-impacting incidents. For Dedicated customers with a contractual SLA, we provide an escalation path to an account engineering lead.

4) Exceptions / planned maintenance flow\- Exception request (Redwood-initiated maintenance or planned deviation):
  * We notify customers at least 72 hours in advance for planned maintenance that could affect SLOs.
  * For emergency exceptions (unplanned work that may temporarily reduce SLOs), we notify within 12 hours with an incident summary and expected impact window.
  * Approval path: for cataloged Planned Exceptions we send a short form (Exception Request) to procurement/security with impact window and rollback plan. Customers sign off by reply or approve via the DocuSign link.

5) Evidence (30-day report)\- Attached: redwood-slo-measurement-overview.pdf (30-day summary, p50/p95/p99, availability). For full raw export we can provide an S3/CSV dump on request or grant read-only dashboard access.

Notes/FAQs:
- For private (VPC/on-prem) deployments we support customer-managed telemetry with the same definitions; reporting cadence is agreed during onboarding.
- Any redacted artifact is possible; we default to tenant-scoped views for privacy.

I've CC'd Jordan (Account Exec) to confirm the contractual/exception approval steps. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if useful.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Director, Technical Sales
Redwood Inference

Samantha — quick practical notes on the approval path and SLAs from our side:

- For Hosted API customers (standard): SLO language is descriptive (targets + measurement window) with credits applied per the T&Cs. Exceptions are documented and recorded but do not require legal amendment for routine planned maintenance; procurement acknowledgement is sufficient.
- For Dedicated/Reserved customers: any SLA exception that affects committed throughput or latency requires written approval from both sides and may trigger a service credit evaluation per the reserved contract.
- Timeline: if Acme needs DocuSign for the exception form we can send a templated PDF within 24 hours.

If you'd like, Marissa (ops lead) can run through what data we include in the 30-day evidence packet (incident timeline, RCA summary, metric blobs).
